angle: mistake hook: buying packs until the album is full costs ~7 albums of stickers; rule out rare stickers (all equally common), the trap is the last page; 670 slots, packs of 5; half the album in ~460 stickers; with 10 left only 1 in 67 is new; the last slot alone 670; re-hook: last 10 slots cost twice the first 500; fix 1: five friends pool and swap -> ~2,000 each; fix 2: order the last 50 -> ~930, under 1,000 each; payoff: the last page is the expensive part; checkable CTA (10-slot album: ~29)
title: Why your sticker album costs 7 albums of stickers
description:
A 670-sticker World Cup album bought from packs alone takes about 4,700 stickers on average (670 x the harmonic number H670), roughly 950 packs. The first half fills with about 460 stickers, but once only 10 slots are left just 1 sticker in 67 is new, and the very last slot takes 670 stickers on its own: the last 10 slots cost twice as much as the first 500. Five friends pooling packs and swapping need about 2,000 stickers each; ordering the last 50 directly brings it to about 930, under 1,000. This is the coupon collector's problem.

Numbers checked in code: exact expected values plus 100,000 simulated albums per case (each sticker equally likely). Album size: Panini FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022, 670 stickers, packs of 5 (The Peninsula / Bloomberg, Aug 2022).
social_caption: Filling a sticker album from packs alone costs about seven albums of stickers. Here's where they all go, and the two fixes that cut it by five.
facts_checked: Panini FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 album: 670 stickers, packets of five (https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/30/08/2022/it-now-costs-1200-on-average-to-complete-world-cup-sticker-album)
Expected draws to complete n equally likely coupons = n x H_n (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coupon_collector%27s_problem); for 670: 4,747 stickers = 7.1 albums = 949 packs (verify.py)
First half (335 slots): 464 stickers; with 10 left a new sticker is 10/670 = 1 in 67; last slot alone 670; last 10 slots 1,962 vs first 500 slots 917, about twice (verify.py)
Simulated 100,000 albums: solo 4,742 on average; 5 friends pooling and swapping 2,010 each; plus each ordering their last 50: 932 each, under 1,000 (verify.py)
CTA answer: a 10-slot album takes 10 x H_10 = 29.3 stickers on average (verify.py)
Panini runs a missing-sticker service for completing albums (https://www.cbsnews.com/video/paninis-missing-sticker-service-helps-world-cup-collectors-complete-their-albums-60-minutes)

beats.say: Fill an album from packs, and you'll buy seven.
It's not rare stickers. Every one is printed equally often. The trap is the last page.
Your World Cup album has 670 slots. Packs come in fives.
At first, almost every sticker is new. Half the album fills with about 460 stickers.
But with 10 slots left, only 1 in 67 stickers is one you need.
The very last slot takes 670 stickers on its own.
So those last 10 slots cost twice as much as the first 500. That's where your money goes.
Fix it. Swap. Your doubles are your friends' gaps. Five friends pooling every pack need about 2,000 stickers each, not 4,700.
Then stop at the last 50 and order them straight from Panini. Now it's under 1,000 each.
The album isn't expensive. The last page is.
So, how many stickers does a 10-slot album take? Guess in the comments.
